builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: VR-SparseQuant: Accurate FP4 Quantization with 2:4 Sparsity on Vera Rubin
summary: VR-SparseQuant replaces dense W4A4 activation quantization with 2:4 structured-sparse FP4 execution on Vera Rubin hardware, using overlapping sparse streams to refine high-error activations while keeping native FP4 throughput. It costs a one-time offline scale-ratio calibration plus custom shared-weight GEMM kernels that only exist for unreleased VRFP4 hardware; the accuracy recovery relative to dense RTN W4A4 is demonstrated on a single model. It can fail on models whose activation error distributions do not align with the 2:4 sparsity pattern, and the perplexity gain does not guarantee downstream task quality.
rationale: The method depends on Vera Rubin's native 2:4 sparse FP4 instructions, which are unavailable on the reader's 24GB GPU or through third-party APIs, so it cannot be adopted or tested today.
technique: 2:4 sparse FP4 activation quantization on Vera Rubin

claims.statement: VR-SparseQuant replaces dense W4A4 activation quantization with 2:4 structured-sparse FP4 execution on Vera Rubin hardware, using overlapping sparse streams to refine high-error activations while keeping native FP4 throughput. It costs a one-time offline scale-ratio calibration plus custom shared-weight GEMM kernels that only exist for unreleased VRFP4 hardware; the accuracy recovery relative to dense RTN W4A4 is demonstrated on a single model. It can fail on models whose activation error distributions do not align with the 2:4 sparsity pattern, and the perplexity gain does not guarantee downstream task quality.
Native VRFP4 kernels achieve up to 3.1x GEMM and 2.7x MoE speedup over BF16, and reduce WikiText-2 perplexity from 6.85 to 5.57 versus dense RTN W4A4 on Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B.
